findings.summary: The demonstrations for the content criteria only read the doc. They have no mechanical check that every J item has a reuse, extend or new tag, or that every question has a number.
findings.evidence: Criteria 2 to 7 all use `git diff -- docs/design/jev-code-health.md` followed by reading. That is acceptable for a prose-only deliverable, but it is easy to skip one field among five questions. Fix: Add a grep check. For example, every build-plan row matches `reuse|extend|new`, and each of the five question headings is followed by a 'Threshold:' line containing a digit.

findings.summary: The plan says Jev's retry goes through gh.rs. This critique did not check that, so the claim should be confirmed before the doc cites it.
findings.evidence: The risks section already says to cite only names the producer has seen. Fix: Producer: read jev.rs and confirm the retry path before naming it in the survey, or leave it out.

summary: I checked the plan's claims against the snapshot and they hold. In crates/athena-core: request_body is at jev.rs:72 and takes a BTreeMap of questions, so several questions fit in one call. FakeJev is at jev.rs:391, live_jev_answers_both_question_kinds at jev.rs:792, and MIN_TEST_CASES and score-jev are in labeled.rs. The CLI test for score-jev is crates/athena-cli/tests/labeled.rs. The two prices are in defaults-loop.md at lines 259 and 667. hestia.md and scope-guard.md both exist. D130 is the last of 130 entries in decisions.md, so appending D131 is right. decision-links.toml is keyed by line numbers, so appending D131 without supersede or amend wording leaves it valid. The plan covers all eight criteria, reuses the existing client, fake and scorer, and keeps every build job to one producer run. The only findings are minor ones about the demonstrations.
